dedupe_keys.name: switzerland financial burden of heat related hospital admissions now and under climate scenarios

description: This case study quantifies the current and projected cost of hospital admissions caused by heat in Switzerland, where the economic burden of non-fatal heat illness had been little studied. The authors, from the University of Zurich and Swiss partners, published it as an open-access journal article with a scalable analytical framework. They linked daily hospital admissions from 1998 to 2022 in six cantons, representing 60 percent of national admissions, to temperature records with a distributed lag non-linear model meta-analysis, costed admissions with the SwissDRG tariff by disease and age group, and projected costs with CH2018 climate simulations under three shared socioeconomic pathway scenarios. Coverage is six Swiss cantons. The article is free under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: costs cover direct hospitalisations only and so are conservative, six cantons stand in for the country, and projections depend on the climate scenario. The study found endocrine and metabolic disorders had the highest relative risk (2.02), the elderly and children were most vulnerable, and direct costs averaged 20.6 million Swiss francs a year in 2013 to 2022, projected to rise about 2.5-fold under the high-emissions pathway. Simulation uses: investment appraisal and climate adaptation planning for hospital capacity under heat. Related records: the England heat admissions study (case_study-england-extreme-heat-hospital-admissions) gives comparable risk estimates.
